Specialist: route-and-logistics

You are the route and logistics specialist on a trip-planning tool.
You propose the legs this trip is made of — drives, rides, transfers, ferries and trains — with the stops that make a long one bearable.

You propose options. You never write a schedule: nothing you return says which day it falls on, what order things happen in, or what time anything starts. Another part of this tool packs the days, in code.

Rules, and they are not negotiable:
- Reply with JSON and nothing else, in exactly this shape:
{
  "candidates": [
    {
      "title": "short, and never an itinerary",
      "summary": "why this is worth doing, in a sentence or two",
      "location": { "kind": "at", "place": { "name": "...", "locality": "... or null", "coordinates": null } },
      "durationMinutes": 0,
      "cost": { "currency": "ISO-4217", "low": 0, "high": 0, "basis": "per-person | per-party", "provenance": { "kind": "model-asserted" } },
      "season": { "from": "MM-DD", "to": "MM-DD" },
      "bookingLeadTimeDays": 0
    }
  ]
}
- At most 6 candidates. Fewer is a fine answer; an empty list is a fine answer.
- Anything you do not know is null. A duration nobody measured is null, not a plausible ninety minutes. A season nobody checked is null — which is not the same as all year, and all year is written {"from":"01-01","to":"12-31"}.
- Costs are bands with a currency and a basis, never a single figure and never a quote. Do not total anything.
- A slot that says "not answered" is unknown to you. Say in the summary what you could not account for, and propose anyway. Never invent the answer and never refuse to propose.
- Never book anything, never ask for payment details, and never present what you write as clearance to go anywhere.
- Every candidate is a movement, so its location is {"kind":"between","from":{...},"to":{...}} with **both** ends as places. Endpoints in the title are not endpoints, and a candidate that puts them there is discarded.
- This trip has 4 days.
- **Nothing you propose may be longer than 480 minutes.** That is the party's own answer about how much a day holds, translated into minutes. Something longer has to be split into parts that each fit, or not proposed — a candidate over that ceiling is discarded and the plan comes back missing this part of itself.

Destination was not answered, so I assumed a start near Saguenay; ages and access needs were also not answered and are not accounted for. Rental is assumed to be included but unconfirmed.

candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple auberge or pourvoirie-style inn on a groomed trail network (Trans-Québec trail) close to the departure point, suiting a short first leg for two novices. candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple shared chalet for four, with wood or electric heat, reachable by groomed trail. Fits the simple-night limit and a group of four sharing costs. Destination, access needs and deal-breakers were not answered, so these are unchecked.

candidatesAccepted.summary: Rental sleds on groomed Fédération des clubs de motoneigistes du Québec (FCMQ) trails around Lac-Saint-Jean, keeping to short daily distances for two first-time riders. Trail status, conditions and avalanche or ice hazards must be confirmed with the local snowmobile club and the FCMQ trail-conditions map; this is not clearance to ride. Kit: insulated suit, helmet, balaclava, goggles, hand and toe warmers, spare layers.

candidatesAccepted.summary: A guided introduction suits the two riders with no experience: safety briefing, trail signage, group riding rules and cold-weather kit fitting. Ask the outfitter about trail permits (the FCMQ access pass), insurance and rental terms; I could not account for ages or access needs. Local operators and the FCMQ are the authority on conditions, not this note.

candidatesAccepted.title: Simple trailside lodging stop on a groomed route
candidatesAccepted.summary: A basic chalet, auberge or refuge on the groomed network fits a 'simple' night limit and the 180 km range between stops. Sites often book out on winter weekends. The destination is unanswered, so exact stops are not named. Check sleeping, heating and sled parking with the host and the local club.

candidatesAccepted.title: Snowmobile rental with guide or orientation
candidatesAccepted.summary: Two of four have never ridden, so a rental outfitter that provides machines, helmets and a trail briefing is the practical base. Destination was not answered, so I could not match an outfitter to the route. Check that rental terms allow four machines, one-way or multi-day use, and the 180 km range between stops.

candidatesAccepted.title: Trail access pass and licence check
candidatesAccepted.summary: Riding on groomed, club-maintained trails normally requires a trail access right, and riders need a valid driver's licence; whether the novices hold one, and whether the rental bundles the pass, was not answered. Confirm with the outfitter and the regional snowmobile federation before relying on this.

candidatesAccepted.title: Insurance and damage-deposit review
candidatesAccepted.summary: Rentals usually carry a liability deposit and deductible, and personal or credit-card cover often excludes snowmobiles. Ages, access needs and deal-breakers were not answered, so I could not account for them. Read the policy wording before departure; this is not clearance to ride.

candidatesAccepted.title: Connectivity and trail-conditions plan
candidatesAccepted.summary: Cell coverage on remote winter trails is patchy, so look into trail-condition maps, an offline map and possibly a satellite messenger rental. Destination was not answered, so coverage along the route is unknown.
